text:
**LiFePO4 (LFP) is the better choice for most people.** Nearly all the sources I found agree on this.

**Where LiFePO4 wins**
- **Cycle life:** LFP stations are typically rated for 3,000-6,000 cycles to 70-80% capacity. NMC units are rated for roughly 500-1,000, and one source says up to 2,000. At one full cycle a day, that's about 8+ years for LFP and under 2-3 years for NMC ([UnpluggedWatts](https://www.unpluggedwatts.com/lifepo4-vs-nmc-power-station/), [OutageMath](https://www.outagemath.com/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc/)).
- **Failure behavior:** In lab tests, LFP cells failed more mildly than NMC cells. They reached lower peak temperatures and gave off smoke rather than flames. The tests were on small cells, and LFP isn't fireproof. It also reached thermal runaway sooner in one overcharge test, so NMC tolerated overcharge better ([UnpluggedWatts](https://www.unpluggedwatts.com/lifepo4-vs-nmc-power-station/), [OutageMath](https://www.outagemath.com/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc/)).
- **Cost over time:** One site's listings show a median of about $0.55/Wh for LFP versus $0.95/Wh for NMC. With the higher cycle ratings, LFP costs much less per cycle ([powerstations.reviews](https://powerstations.reviews/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc)).
- **Availability:** Most current models are LFP. NMC is mostly in older stock, compact units and clearance ([OutageMath](https://www.outagemath.com/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc/)).

**Where NMC wins**
- NMC cells hold more energy per kilogram. But in finished power stations the gap shrinks, because the case, inverter and fans weigh the same either way. One database found the median NMC station only about 10% denser, and one LFP unit was lighter per Wh than an NMC one ([OutageMath](https://www.outagemath.com/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc/), [UnpluggedWatts](https://www.unpluggedwatts.com/lifepo4-vs-nmc-power-station/)).

**Caveats**
- **Cycle claims:** Compare the end point (70% vs 80%) and the test conditions, not just the number ([Enough Watts](https://enoughwatts.com/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc)).
- **Cold weather:** Cold charging depends more on the maker than the chemistry. Most stations of both types won't charge below 32°F, so check the manual ([powerstations.reviews](https://powerstations.reviews/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc)). Some sources claim LFP handles cold much better, but others contradict that.
- **Occasional use:** If you only use it a few times a year for outages, cycle count matters less, since the battery will age with time first.

**When to pick NMC:** Only if you need the lightest possible unit, or you find a steep discount on a unit you'll use rarely. If you already own a working NMC unit, keep using it.

**Example LiFePO4 pick:** The BLUETTI Elite 200 V2 has 2,073.6 Wh, a 2,600 W inverter and a 6,000+ cycle rating, with a 5-year warranty. It isn't expandable. The list price is $899, or $854.05 with code AFF5OFF, which the source tested in BLUETTI's cart on 2026-10-24. [Buy at BLUETTI's US store](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-elite-200-v2). This is an affiliate link, so the site earns a commission at no cost to you. Checkout has the final say on price ([Dealectric listing](https://dealectric.com/bluetti-elite-200-v2)).

Choose a unit by whether it can run your appliances first, using wattage and capacity, and by chemistry second.
